details:
Grist is spreadsheet software using Python as its formula language. Grist offers several methods for running those formulas in a sandbox, for cases where the user may be working with untrusted spreadsheets. One such method runs them in pyodide, but pyodide on node does not have a useful sandbox barrier.

### Impact
If a user of Grist sets `GRIST_SANDBOX_FLAVOR` to `pyodide` and opens a malicious document, that document could run arbitrary processes on the server hosting Grist.

### Patches
The problem has been addressed in Grist version 1.7.9 and up, by running pyodide under deno.

### Workarounds
A user can use the gvisor-based sandbox by setting  `GRIST_SANDBOX_FLAVOR` to `gvisor` as documented at https://support.getgrist.com/self-managed/#how-do-i-sandbox-documents

### Credit
Thanks to @VladimirEliTokarev for drawing our attention to this weakness.
